name: Lip implants (Permalip, Gore-Tex)
lead: Lip implants are solid, permanent inserts placed in the lips to increase volume. Two materials are most discussed: expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE, sold as Gore-Tex and similar products) and solid silicone (Permalip) [1][2].

ePTFE implants were used for lip and wrinkle augmentation from the early 1990s. A 1992 report described permanent augmentation with PTFE grafts [3], and a 2002 paper noted complications including infection, extrusion, migration, shrinkage and hardening in some patients and tested a newly designed ePTFE implant [4]. A 2017 retrospective study of 100 women reported on solid lip prostheses [5].
Use has declined relative to fillers; a 2006 survey article asked who was still using lip implants [6].

paras: ePTFE has a porous structure that tissue can grow into, and was placed as strips or tubes [2][7]. Grokipedia describes Permalip as a soft solid silicone elastomer, 3-5 mm thick and 55-65 mm long, inserted through small incisions at the mouth corners [7]. Details come from an unverified source.

The 1992 report described the lack of reliable techniques using the patient's own tissue and reluctance to place implants in so exposed an area, then reported PTFE as a predictable permanent option [3]. By 2002 ePTFE had been used for more than ten years [4].

A 2002 study assessed short-term results and complications of a redesigned ePTFE implant for lips, nasolabial folds and marionette lines [4]. A 2017 retrospective study treated 100 women with atrophic or hypoplastic lips using solid prostheses and presented tips for technique [5]. Grokipedia cites a five-year study of 420 patients in which 25.4 percent moved from thin to normal lip classification [7], which was not verified. A 2023 StatPearls chapter gives an overview [8]. Scoping review literature also covers surgical remodeling after permanent filler injection, a related category [9].
ePTFE complications reported include infection, extrusion, migration, shrinkage and hardening [4]. Wikipedia lists implant movement and extrusion among lip augmentation complications [2].

card.summary: Permanent solid inserts (Gore-Tex or silicone) for lip volume; durable but with extrusion and migration risks.
card.note: Implants can extrude or migrate; removal may be needed.

quick.overview:
Lip implants are solid strips or tubes placed in the lip for permanent volume, made of ePTFE (Gore-Tex) or silicone.

Studies are mostly case series. Fillers are now more commonly used.
quick.mechanism: The implant sits in or near the lip muscle and adds bulk. ePTFE is porous so tissue grows in.
quick.risks: Reported complications include infection, extrusion, migration, shrinkage and hardening; removal may be required.
